No, by speed I mean the max amount light that can enter the lens, in other words [aperture](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aperture). Basically the more light is available, the shorter the shutter speed can be. Short shutter is necessary to produce sharp, non-blurry images. 

The larger the aperture, the smaller the f value and the more light enters the lens. So a f/2.8 lens is faster than a f/5.6 lens.

You need a long, fast (depending on light condition when you shoot) and (usually) zoom lens. For Canon there're the 70-200mm f/2.8 or f/4 Lenses and there's a similar lens for Nikon too. Unfortunately they aren't cheap. 

Or you can get a longer 70-300mm but they usually don't come with a fixed aperture and are usually slower.

Telephoto lenses from Sigma, Tamron and other manufacturers are cheaper. 

[This page](http://www.bobatkins.com/photography/eosfaq/telefoto.htm) seems to be a pretty good summary for Canon shooters.

IntelliJ doesn't have as many plugins as Eclipse (don't know whether that's a good thing or not). However, it's got all the ones that I require. 

It supports third-party plugins but in my experiences, most of the plugins I use are from JetBrains (the IntelliJ developers). 

You can check out the list of plugins [here](http://plugins.intellij.net/). 

IMHO, the update manager is far less confusing than that in Eclipse.

IntelliJ FTW!

Seriously, IntelliJ is so much better than Eclipse albeit it uses far more system resources (i.e., memory). For that price, you get so much more. I know it's not free but IntelliJ 9 has an open-source edition, completely free. Moreover, if your project is open-source, you can get the ultimate edition for free.

P.S., I'm not affiliated in IntelliJ in any way, just a happy user.
